name: aware-datetime-compare
diff:
diff --git a/app/tokens.py b/app/tokens.py
--- a/app/tokens.py
+++ b/app/tokens.py
@@ -1,6 +1,6 @@
-from datetime import datetime
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
 
 
 def is_expired(token):
     # token.expires_at comes from the database as an aware UTC datetime
-    return token.expires_at < datetime.now()
+    return token.expires_at < datetime.now(timezone.utc)

question.prompt: expires_at is a timezone-aware UTC datetime. What happened when the old is_expired ran, and what does passing timezone.utc change?
question.answerKey: datetime.now() returns a naive datetime, and Python refuses to order an aware datetime against a naive one, so the old code raised TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes. datetime.now(timezone.utc) is aware and in UTC, so the comparison works and both sides are in the same zone.
rubric: comparing the aware expires_at with the naive datetime.now() raised a TypeError
now(timezone.utc) gives an aware UTC time, so the comparison is valid and in the same zone

answers.text: TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes. Passing timezone.utc makes now() aware and UTC so the < works.
the old one blew up (naive vs aware compare). now both sides are aware UTC
It worked but was off by the server's UTC offset, so tokens expired early or late.
It always returned False, because naive datetimes compare as earlier.
